evals.name: linear-algebra-ml
evals.prompt: I'm a software engineer, mid-30s. I've been coding professionally for 10+ years, mostly Python and distributed systems stuff. I took calculus in college but honestly barely remember anything beyond basic derivatives. I've never formally studied linear algebra and it's biting me now — I'm trying to get more into ML/AI work, and every time I read a paper the math section stops me cold. Matrix operations, SVD, eigenvectors, that whole world. I want to get to the point where I can read an ML paper and actually follow the math, and where I know what I'm doing when I write numpy code instead of just copying from stackoverflow. I can commit about 45 minutes on weekdays, maybe a bit more on weekends. No hard deadline but I'd like to feel real progress within a month or two. Where do I start and what should my plan look like?
evals.expected_output: A concrete phased learning plan with daily session structure, specific resources, feedback/assessment mechanism, and anti-patterns tailored to this learner

evals.name: cant-stick-with-learning
evals.prompt: ok so i have a real problem. last year i decided i was going to learn spanish and i did duolingo for like 3 months and i watched a bunch of youtube videos and i felt like i was making progress but then i went on a trip to mexico and realized i literally couldnt understand or say anything useful. earlier this year i tried to pick up piano, bought a keyboard, watched some videos, tried to learn this one chopin piece because it sounded cool, and now the keyboard is sitting in the corner. like every time i start something i get really excited and watch a ton of videos and it feels like im learning but then a few weeks in i realize i cant actually do anything and i get discouraged and quit. whats wrong with how im approaching this and how do i actually learn a new skill without this happening again? im open to specific advice.
evals.expected_output: Diagnosis of the passive-consumption / no-active-practice / no-retrieval pattern, plus principles and a concrete template for how to approach a new skill

evals.name: chess-1500
evals.prompt: help me plan out how to get good at chess. im around 800 elo on lichess rapid right now. goal is to hit 1500 by end of the year — its april so thats 8-9 months. i can realistically do 30-45 min a day most days. i know basic rules and very basic tactics (pins, forks, that kinda thing). i have no idea what to actually spend my time on — should i be doing puzzles, playing games, studying openings, watching streamers, reading a book, something else? whats the actual plan
evals.expected_output: A specific, phased chess improvement plan with daily session structure, feedback mechanisms, and rationale for each activity
